Documentation → Releases → 2.12.0

SATOM 2.12.0

Templates now know which firmware build they were written for and are checked against every target build, predefined protection profiles are cached in a factory catalog, and deep rediscovery is much faster.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • What's new
  • Templates record their firmware build
  • Every apply is checked against the target's build
  • Approval covers specific builds
  • Adapt to firmware
  • Factory catalog for predefined protection profiles
  • What changes for you
  • Deep rediscovery with the CLI capture is much faster
  • Before you upgrade
  • Learn more

Released: 2026-10-06 · All releases

In short#

2.12.0 closes a quiet gap: a FortiWeb accepts a write containing a field its build does not know, reports success and simply drops the field. Templates now record the firmware build they belong to and are checked against each target's build before they are applied. The release also introduces the factory catalog, which stops SATOM from re-reading the same vendor-written protection profiles on every sweep, and makes a deep rediscovery with the CLI capture much faster.

Anyone who applies templates or runs rediscoveries will notice the change. Administrators should read Before you upgrade: approved templates need one click to be rolled out again.

What's new#

Templates record their firmware build#

Templates now store the firmware build their content was written for, the REST API version, where they came from (captured from an appliance, written by hand, or adapted) and, for captures, the source appliance.

  • Save as template (from a Web Protection Profile or a configuration object) records the appliance's running build.
  • New Template, the New template form on section pages and System Provisioning now ask you to choose a build SATOM knows. System profiles no longer default to a fixed "8.0" line.
  • When you save, the template is compared with its own build through the API library, and the Template Library shows whether it fits.

Every apply is checked against the target's build#

Every way of applying a template — the Template Library, section pages, System Provisioning, baselines, and the automatic fleet deploy after a Web Protection Profile is approved — now shows a verdict per device:

  • fields the build would discard, renamed fields and endpoints the build does not serve block the apply;
  • missing evidence is a warning, never a pass;
  • an approver can override with a reason, and the override is audited.

Approval covers specific builds#

Approving a template now records the builds it was validated for. Rolling it out to the fleet on another build needs Revalidate first.

Adapt to firmware#

Adapt to firmware saves a new pending version of a template rewritten for a target build: known renames are carried over, fields the build does not serve are removed, and every change is listed in the version note.

See Template library.

Factory catalog for predefined protection profiles#

Every FortiWeb ships the same twenty or so predefined Web Protection Profiles, and the deep pass used to read all of them in full on every appliance, on every sweep — up to about 125 device reads each, most of the sweep's work. SATOM now keeps them in a factory catalog, one entry per profile per firmware version, build number and REST API version.

  • The first deep pass on a build reads the predefined profiles in full and stores them.
  • Later deep passes rebuild a predefined profile from the catalog, but only when the appliance's own rows match the stored entry. Anything that does not match is read in full, as before. The appliance's own usage counters are kept.
  • Entries are re-read in full once a week by default, or on demand with the new Re-read predefined WPPs in full switch on the Rediscovery page.
  • If two appliances on the same build disagree below matching rows, the entry is marked ambiguous and that profile is always read in full on that build. A failed read is never stored.
  • The firmware is read live from the appliance at the start of the deep pass, not from the appliance record, which can be empty.
  • The Rediscovery page reports how many predefined profiles came from the catalog.

The new Factory catalog page (linked from Web Protection and the Template Library) lists the builds and each profile's full content, compares the same profile between two builds field by field, and saves an entry as a template, stamped with its firmware and API version and marked as coming from the factory; it then goes through the usual approval. Viewing the page needs View registry. See Factory catalog.

What changes for you#

Deep rediscovery with the CLI capture is much faster#

A deep rediscovery with protection profiles and the CLI capture was reported as extremely slow. The captured configuration is the same; how it is read changed:

  • Each device read happens once per sweep. A protection profile shared by 30 policies used to be read 31 times; repeated reads are now answered from memory. The finished sweep reports how many device reads it made and how many were reused.
  • The CLI capture runs alongside the deep pass, so the sweep takes as long as the longer of the two instead of their sum. If you press Stop during the deep pass, a capture already running is allowed to finish.
  • Up to 3 reads run at once per appliance during the endpoint sweep and the deep pass. Progress and results are unchanged. Parallel reads start only after the credentials are confirmed, and after an authentication refusal SATOM pauses new reads until a single re-check answers, so a lockout costs very few extra attempts. FortiADC stays one read at a time.
  • One connection is reused per sweep instead of a new secure connection for every request.

The Stop label on the Rediscovery page now names the CLI capture when that is the step still running. See Discovery and rediscovery.

Before you upgrade#

  • Templates saved before this release show no firmware.
  • Approved templates have no validated builds yet. Their fleet rollouts and baseline applies are refused until an approver clicks Revalidate for fleet builds (in the template's View dialog), once per template.
  • Single-device applies are only checked field by field and keep working.
  • The factory catalog and the parallel reads can be tuned or switched off by your administrator in the node configuration; see Configuration files and environment variables.
